results.title: Used EV Prices Surpass Gasoline Cars: Compact Models Drive the Shift
results.description: The average price of used electric vehicles (EVs) in the U. S. has surpassed that of internal combustion engine (ICE) vehicles for the first time in a year, according to data from iSeeCars. In September 2026, the average price for a used EV between one and five years old was $32,533, compared to $31,954 for gasoline-powered equivalents. This $579 premium marks a significant reversal from September 2025, when used EVs were, on average, $2,227 cheaper than their gasoline counterparts. Liquidity and Segment Divergence The price increase is accompanied by higher liquidity. Used EVs spent an average of 41.9 days on dealer lots, notably faster than gasoline vehicles (54.8 days) and hybrids (48.6 days). However, this demand is not uniform across the market. High liquidity is concentrated in affordable, compact models: the Audi Q4 Sportback E-Tron, Toyota bZ4X, and Lexus RZ 300e averaged between 29.8 and 34.3 days on the lot. Conversely, high-end electric trucks and SUVs continue to struggle with slower turnover. The Cadillac Escalade IQ averaged 128.7 days on the lot, while the GMC Sierra EV and Chevrolet Silverado EV spent 93.2 and 89.1 days, respectively. These figures suggest that the current market recovery is driven by the mass-market segment rather than premium luxury EVs.
